### A {#A}

#### Anchored fish aggregating device (AFAD) {#anchoredFishanchoredAggregatinganchoredDevice}

A device tethered to the bottom of the ocean usually consisting of a buoy-and anchored to the bottom of the ocean (IOTC Resolution 23/01).


Device that is anchored or otherwise attached to the seabed and is used for attracting and concentrating fish for the purpose of capture by a fishing gear (FAO terminology portal).

#### Ancillary logs {#ancillaryLogs}

Data records from the electronic monitoring (EM) system that are supplemental to the EM Records such as a record of changes in system configurations and settings and a summary of system health checks performed (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Aquascope {#aquascope}

A device that allows looking underwater from the surface, made of a cylinder or a cone, closed at both ends by a glass. Also called a bathyscope (IOTC ROS data standards).

#### Areas beyond national jurisdiction (ABNJ) {#areasBeyondareasNationalareasJurisdiction}

Commonly called the high seas- are those areas of ocean for which no one nation has sole responsibility for management (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Artificial Intelligence (AI) {#artificialIntelligence}

A machine-based system that can - for a given set of human- defined objectives -  make predictions - recommendations or decisions influencing real or virtual environments. Artificial intelligence systems use machine and human-based inputs to (A) perceive real and virtual environments; (B) abstract such perceptions into models through analysis in an automated matter; and (C) use model inference to formulate options for information or action (Murua 2025 EM workshop- WPCFC).

#### Artisanal fishery {#artisanalFishery}

Traditional fishery that involves fishing households (as opposed to commercial companies) - using relatively small amounts of capital and energy - relatively small fishing vessels (if any) - making short fishing trips close to shore - mainly for local consumption. In practice - definition varies between countries - e.g. from gleaning or a one-man canoe in poor developing countries - to more than 20 m trawlers - seiners or longliners in developed ones. Artisanal fisheries can be subsistence or commercial fisheries, providing for local consumption or export. They are sometimes referred to as small-scale fisheries (https://www.fao.org/documents/card/en/c/ae76ef51-be20-5e71-aec5-b469e5e0a673).


Fishery composed of fishing vessels of less than 24 m length overall that exclusively operate in the exclusive economic zone of their flag state (tbd).

#### Artisanal fishing vessel {#artisanalFishingartisanalVessel}

Fishing vessel less than 24 m in length overall operating inside the exclusive economic zone of a flag State and catching tuna or tuna-like species in the IOTC area of competence. Synonym to coastal fishing vessel (Guidelines for the reporting of fishery statistics to the IOTC).

#### Associated school {#associatedSchool}

The fish school is associated with a topographic structure (e.g., seamount), an anchored or a drifting floating object, including man-made rafts such as fish aggregating devices and live animals in motion (e.g., whale sharks, cetaceans) (Guidelines for the reporting of fishery statistics to the IOTC).

#### Astronomical Twilight {#astronomicalTwilight}

The period before sunrise or after sunset when the centre of the Sun is 18� below the horizon, marking the limit of twilight before full darkness or daylight (Based on U.S. Naval Observatory's Astronomical Almanac glossary).

#### At-surface setting {#atSurfaceatSetting}

The gear is deployed at the surface of the water (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Authorised vessel {#authorisedVessel}

Any vessel that is: a) 24 meters in length overall or above; or b) in the case of vessels less than 24 meters in length overall, those operating outside areas under the national jurisdiction of the flag State, and is authorised by the flag State to fish for tuna and tuna-like species or to carry out fishing related activities in the IOTC Area of Competence (IOTC definition).

#### Auto pilot {#autoPilot}

An automatic steering system that maintains a vessel on a predetermined heading or course without continuous manual control (IMO International Maritime Dictionary).

#### Automatic Identification System (AIS) {#automaticIdentificationautomaticSystem}

A maritime communication and identification system that automatically transmits and receives information, including a vessel's identity, position, course, speed and other navigational information, between equipped vessels and shore-based stations (International Maritime Organization (IMO Safety of Navigation)).

### B {#B}

#### Bait casting {#baitCasting}

The process of manually or mechanically throwing or placing baited hooks into the water during the setting of fishing gear (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Beach seine {#beachSeine}

A seine net operated from the shore, in which the net is set from a boat or by wading and then hauled back to the beach to encircle and capture fish (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Brailer {#brailer}

A bag-shaped net or scoop used to transfer fish from a fishing gear or holding area into a vessel or container (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Bridge/wheelhouse {#bridgeWheelhouse}

The area of a vessel from which navigation, manoeuvring, and control of the vessel are conducted (IMO terminology).

#### Bycatch {#bycatch}

All species, other than the 16 species listed in Annex B of the IOTC Agreement, caught or interacted with by fisheries for tuna and tuna-like species in the IOTC area of competence. A bycatch species includes those non-IOTC species which are (a) retained (byproduct), (b) incidentally taken in a fishery and returned to the sea (discarded); or (c) incidentally affected by interacting with fishing equipment in the fishery, but not taken (IOTC Agreement).

#### Byproduct {#byproduct}

A non-target species or material retained from a fishing operation that has economic or other value but is not the primary target of the fishery (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

### C {#C}

#### Call sign {#callSign}

A unique combination of letters and/or numbers assigned to a vessel or radio station for identification during radio communications (IMO terminology).

#### Cast nets {#castNets}

Fishing gear cast from the shore or from a boat over the water surface; catches the fish by falling and closing in on them by means of a drawstring. Its use is usually restricted to shallow waters, (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Chafer {#chafer}

A protective section of netting or material attached to areas of a fishing net, particularly a purse seine, that are subject to abrasion to reduce wear and damage (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Chartering state {#charteringState}

A Contracting Party or Cooperating Non-Contracting Party of the IOTC that has been granted the right to use a vessel flying the flag of another State for fishing activities under a charter arrangement (IOTC).

#### Civil twilight {#civilTwilight}

The period between sunset and when the Sun is 6� below the horizon, and between sunrise and when the Sun rises to 6� below the horizon, when natural light is still available (Revised from US Naval Observatory).

#### Cleithrum-fork length {#cleithrumForkcleithrumLength}

Straight distance between the cleithrum and the fork of the tail (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Cleithrum-keel length {#cleithrumKeelcleithrumLength}

Straight distance between the cleithrum and the anterior insertion of the caudal keel (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Coastal fishery {#coastalFishery}

Any fishery, including artisanal fisheries, where the fishing activity is undertaken by a vessel below 24 m length overall that is not required to be registered on the IOTC Record of Authorised Vessels (IOTC-2025-CoC22-11_Add4-IOTC Glossary).

#### Commercial fishery {#commercialFishery}

A fishery conducted for commercial purposes, where the catch is intended for sale or trade (IOTC glossary).

#### Commercial small scale fisheries {#commercialSmallcommercialScalecommercialFisheries}

Fish caught in national jurisdiction areas (NJA) of the flag state, by vessels with a length overall of less than 15 m, and sold at landing sites, at markets, to processing factories (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Conservation and management measure {#conservationAndconservationManagementconservationMeasure}

Any measure adopted pursuant to Articles V(2)(c) and IX in the IOTC Agreement, and more generally where not applicable to IOTC such measures that are consistent with international law (IOTC guidelines for reporting fisheries statistics).

#### Control centre/box {#controlCentrecontrolBox}

The electronic monitoring (EM) control centre is a computer and software system that records and stores information from EM System components (e.g., video, sensor data, GPS data) (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Course {#course}

The direction in which a vessel is intended to be steered, expressed as the horizontal angle measured clockwise from true north (IMO terminology).

### D {#D}

#### Danish seines {#danishSeines}

A seine fishing gear consisting of a net with long ropes used to encircle fish on the seabed; the ropes are hauled to herd the fish into the net, which is then retrieved onto the vessel (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Data storage backup* {#dataStoragedataBackup}

The electronic monitoring (EM) equipment should include separate, duplicate backup devices to ensure that data are not lost if a storage device fails (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Data storage* {#dataStorage}

The electronic monitoring (EM) equipment should have enough storage capacity to store all EM records for a certain period of time, which should be at minimum a complete trip. The duration will depend on the vessel's operational characteristics that could range from 4 months (in the case of purse seiners) to 12 months or more in the case of longliners) (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Deactivation of a buoy {#deactivationOfdeactivationAdeactivationBuoy}

The process of disabling a buoy's operational functions, such as transmission of location or status information, so that it is no longer active for tracking or marking fishing gear (adapted from IOTC terms).

#### Deep setting* {#deepSetting}

The gear is deployed in deep waters (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Demersal setting* {#demersalSetting}

The gear is set in waters close to the seabed (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Depredation {#depredation}

An interaction between marine animals (e.g. cetaceans, seabirds, sea turtles, sharks and rays) with different types of fishing gear considered to be a source of food. Depredatory behaviour can have consequences on fisheries through the removal of bait or caught fish from hooks, nets or traps, thereby reducing commercial catches (i.e. income) or damage done to fishing gear. Depredation can also impact animals (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Designated installer or service technician {#designatedInstallerdesignatedOrdesignatedServicedesignatedTechnician}

A person or entity authorised by en EM Service provider to install or service an EM system,Designated installer or service technician (Marua 2025-WCPFC term).

#### Digital selective calling (DSC) {#digitalSelectivedigitalCalling}

A radio communication system that uses digital signals to automatically transmit and receive distress alerts and other calls between maritime radio stations (IMO terminology).


A component of GMDSS: The IMO also introduced Digital Selective Calling (DSC) on MF, HF and VHF maritime radios as part of the GMDSS system. Each DSC-equipped ship (observer manual 2019).

#### Discards* {#discards}

All non-retained catch, including individuals released alive or discarded dead (IOTC science glossary).


the part of the catch that is not retained on board and is returned at sea (FAO terminology portal).

#### Doppler current meter {#dopplerCurrentdopplerMeter}

An acoustic instrument that measures water current velocity and direction by detecting the Doppler shift of reflected sound waves (Based on - RD Instruments (RDI). (1996). Acoustic Doppler Current Profilers: Principles of Operation - A Practical Primer. Teledyne RD Instruments.).

#### Drifting fish aggregating device (DFAD) {#driftingFishdriftingAggregatingdriftingDevice}

Fish aggregating device not tethered to the bottom of the ocean typically composed of a floating structure (such as a bamboo or metal raft with buoyancy provided by buoys, corks, etc.) and of a submerged structure (made of canvass, etc.) (IOTC reporting guidelines glossary).


device that is neither anchored nor otherwise attached to the seabed and let adrift (FAO terminology portal).

#### Drifting gillnet {#driftingGillnet}

A gillnet that is not attached to the seabed and is allowed to drift freely with currents, usually at or near the surface, to entangle fish (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Drifting longline {#driftingLongline}

Longline kept near the surface or at a certain depth by means of regularly spaced floats. Drifting longlines may be of considerable length, and the snoods are usually longer and more widely spaced than for the bottom longlines. Some drifting longlines are set vertically, each line hanging from a float at the surface. They are usually worked in groups of several lines operated by a single boat (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

### E {#E}

#### Echosounder {#echosounder}

Transducer located beneath the hull transmits a sound wave downwards which is reflected on the bottom (echo) to return to the hull and indicate the depth of water. The sound waves are reflected also from fish and can help the captain to spot the schools of fish. The depth on an echo sounder can be measured either in meters (m) or fathoms (fm) (based on IEC definition (from observer manual)).

#### Effort {#effort}

A measure of the resources used to harvest a fishery's stock. The measure of effort appropriate for a fishery depends on the methods used and the management arrangements. Common measures include the number of vessels (IOTC science glossary).

#### Electronic compass {#electronicCompass}

A navigational instrument that determines and displays a vessel's heading using electronic sensors rather than a magnetic needle (IMO termonology).

#### Electronic monitoring analysis {#electronicMonitoringelectronicAnalysis}

The review of electronic monitoring (EM) records by EM observers/reviewers to produce EM data (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic monitoring analyst {#electronicMonitoringelectronicAnalyst}

Electronic monitoring (EM) reviewer / observer -- a person qualified to review EM records (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic monitoring certifier {#electronicMonitoringelectronicCertifier}

An individual or organisation which has been approved by the appropriate authority to inspect and approve EM systems for use (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic monitoring coverage* {#electronicMonitoringelectronicCoverage}

The proportion of vessels or fishing effort that are recorded by the electronic monitoring programme (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic monitoring data {#electronicMonitoringelectronicData}

Processed/analysed data produced through review of electronic monitoring (EM) records that conforms with the EM data standards (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic monitoring data standards {#electronicMonitoringelectronicDataelectronicStandards}

The agreed subset of data requirements by the IOTC Regional Observer Scheme that could be collected by the electronic monitoring system (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic monitoring equipment {#electronicMonitoringelectronicEquipment}

A network of electronic cameras (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic monitoring event {#electronicMonitoringelectronicEvent}

An occurrence in the electronic monitoring records that is enumerated into electronic monitoring data (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic monitoring installation coverage {#electronicMonitoringelectronicInstallationelectronicCoverage}

The proportion of vessels by fleet that has EM equipment installed that is operational,Electronic monitoring installation coverage (IOTC Resolution 23/08).

#### Electronic monitoring observer/reviewer {#electronicMonitoringelectronicObserverelectronicReviewer}

A person qualified to review EM records (IOTC Resolution 23/08).

#### Electronic monitoring observer/reviewer coverage {#electronicMonitoringelectronicObserverelectronicReviewerelectronicCoverage}

The proportion of fishing effort for which EM records are reviewed to produce EM data and submitted to the IOTC (IOTC Resolution 23/08).

#### Electronic monitoring process* {#electronicMonitoringelectronicProcess}

** recommendation from EM workshop to use this instead of EM system.

#### Electronic monitoring programme {#electronicMonitoringelectronicProgramme}

A process administered by a national or regional administration that regulates the use of electronic monitoring systems (EMS) on vessel to collect and verify fisheries data and information responsible throgh an implementation of an EMS in a defined area and/or fishery (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic monitoring record coverage {#electronicMonitoringelectronicRecordelectronicCoverage}

The proportion of fishing effort for which EM records are collected by installed EM equipment (Resolution 23/08).


The percentage of total fishing effort (trips/events) for which EM records are available,Electronic monitoring record coverage.

#### Electronic monitoring records {#electronicMonitoringelectronicRecords}

Electronic data (footage and other information such as ancillary data and metadata) captured during a fishing trip (Murua et al. 2025).


Imagery, and possibly sensor, raw data linked to positional data collected by an EM equipment that can be reviewed to produce EM data.

#### Electronic monitoring review centre {#electronicMonitoringelectronicReviewelectronicCentre}

A designated facility responsible for reviewing and analysing electronic monitoring records (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic monitoring review provider {#electronicMonitoringelectronicReviewelectronicProvider}

A third-party provider of electronic monitoring (EM) review services to review EM records to produce EM data. The same third-party organisation can provide both the EM equipment and EM review services but they can also be supplied by different providers (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic monitoring review rate {#electronicMonitoringelectronicReviewelectronicRate}

The proportion of EM records that are analysed to produce EM data (WCPFC).

#### Electronic monitoring system (EMS) {#electronicMonitoringelectronicSystem}

An integrated system of hardware and software that supports acquisition of video footages of fishing activity, positional data and/or sensor (Resolution 25/06).


The system comprising the vessel and shore- based components for collecting, transmitting and reviewing EM records (EM workshop Marua 2025-IOTC).

#### Electronic monitoring user interface {#electronicMonitoringelectronicUserelectronicInterface}

A display that communicates electronic monitoring system status messages and provides views of onboard cameras (EM workshop-WCPFC term only).

#### Electronic monitoring* (EM) {#electronicMonitoring}

The use of electronic devices to record fishing vessels' activities using video technology linked to a global navigation satellite system (Murua et al. 2025).

#### Electronic technologies {#electronicTechnologies}

Any electronic tool that is used to support fisheries-dependent data collection, both on shore and at sea (Resolution 23/08).

#### Emergency position-indicating radio beacon (EPIRB) {#emergencyPositionemergencyIndicatingemergencyRadioemergencyBeacon}

A satellite-based distress beacon carried by ships that transmits an alert containing the vessel's identity and location to assist search and rescue authorities in locating a vessel in an emergency (IMO terminology).

#### Encircling gillnets {#encirclingGillnets}

An encircling gillnet is a gillnet set vertical, in shallow waters, encircling fish. After the fish has been encircled by the net, noise or other means are used to force them to gill or entangle themselves in the netting. It is a technology commonly used by groups of small-scale fishermen (or women) (Gear code lists).

#### Engine power {#enginePower}

The maximum continuous power output of a vessel's engine, usually expressed in kilowatts (kW) or horsepower (hp) (based on IMO terminology).

#### Engine room {#engineRoom}

A compartment or space in a ship containing the main propulsion machinery and associated equipment required for the operation of the vessel (IMO terminology).

#### Exclusive economic zone (EEZ) {#exclusiveEconomicexclusiveZone}

A zone under national jurisdiction (up to 200-nautical miles wide) declared in line with the provisions of 1982 United Nations Convention of the Law of the Sea, within which the coastal State has the right to explore and exploit, and the responsibility to conserve and manage, the living and non-living resources (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).


An area beyond and adjacent to the territorial sea, subject to the specific legal regime established in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, which provides that it is not to extend beyond 200 nm from the baselines from which the breadth of the territorial sea is measured (IOTC data reporting guidelines).

#### Exhaustive sampling {#exhaustiveSampling}

All individuals in the catch or sampling unit are examined and recorded (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Expendable Bathythermograph (XBT) {#expendableBathythermograph}

A small, single-use probe dropped from a moving ship to measure ocean temperature down the water column.

### F {#F}

#### Field sampler {#fieldSampler}

A person who collects information on land during the unloading of fishing vessels and field sampling programs can be used inter alia for quantifying catch (Resolution 25/06).

#### Fish aggregating device (FAD) {#fishAggregatingfishDevice}

Artificial or natural floating objects placed on the ocean surface, often anchored to the bottom, to attract several schooling fish species underneath (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).


Anchored, drifting, floating, swimming or submerged object or group of objects, of any size,
that has or has not been deployed, that is living or non-living, including but not limited to buoys, floats, netting, webbing, plastics,
bamboo, logs, whales and whale sharks that fish may associate with.. See also Anchored FAD and Drifting FAD (IOTC science glossary).

#### Fisher {#fisher}

an individual who engages in fishing activities for the purpose of deriving a livelihood, generating a revenue or pursuing sport or recreation (IOTC data reporting guidelines).

#### Fishery {#fishery}

An activity leading to harvesting of fish. It may involve capture of wild fish or raising of fish through aquaculture ([FAO fishery glossary](https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)),Fishery (FAO) (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Fishery information system* (FIS) {#fisheryInformationfisherySystem}

#### Fishing capacity* {#fishingCapacity}

The ability of a vessel or fleet of vessels to catch fish. Fishing capacity (capacity output) can be expressed more specifically as the maximum amount of fish over a period of time (year, season) that can be produced by a fishing fleet if fully utilised (Github glossary).


(1) The potential fishing effort that could be exerted in a fishery, over a period of time (year, season) if all fishers are participating and all vessels and gear are fully used. (2) The maximum amount of fish that could be taken in a fishery or by a single fishing unit (e.g. a fisher, community, vessel or fleet) over a period of time (season, year), given the biomass and age structure of the fish stock and the present state of the technology (FAO terminology portal).

#### Fishing effort {#fishingEffort}

The overall amount of fishing (usually per unit of time) expressed in units such as: boat days on the fishing ground, number of traps, or trawl hauls, or (gillnet length x soaking time) (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).


amount of fishing taking place, usually described in terms of gear type and the frequency or period of operations (e.g. 'hook sets', 'trawl hours', 'searching hours') (IOTC glossary scientific terms).

#### Fishing effort (effective) {#fishingEffortfishingEffective}

Adjusted measure of effort to take account of differences in fishing power and efficiency and ensure proportionality with fishing mortality, and when two or more kinds of gear are used or when the same gear is used for example by different classes of vessel or m�tier, the respective efforts are adjusted to some common standard before being aggregated across all classes (strata) ([CWP Handbook](https://www.fao.org/cwp-on-fishery-statistics/handbook/en/)) (IOTC glossary).

#### Fishing effort (nominal) {#fishingEffortfishingNominal}

General measure of effort used to quantify the unadjusted, total effort units exerted on a stock in a given time period by a fishery (IOTC glossary).

#### Fishing event* {#fishingEvent}

#### Fishing gear {#fishingGear}

The general name for the equipment used for fishing. This might include lines, nets, warps, floats, deck equipment and any other specific fishing items (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Fishing logbook {#fishingLogbook}

A paper based or electronic record of any data related to fishing or fishing related activities (IOTC-2025-CoC22-11_Add4-IOTC Glossary).

#### Fishing master* {#fishingMaster}

A person responsible for managing and directing fishing operations on board a fishing vessel, including decisions related to fishing methods, gear deployment, and catch operations (need a reference).

#### Fishing mode {#fishingMode}

A specific practice or method of conducting a fishing operation or searching for fish within a fishery (github glossary).

#### Fishing related activities {#fishingRelatedfishingActivities}

Any operation in support of, or in preparation for, fishing, including the landing, packaging, processing, transhipping or transporting of fish that have not been previously landed at a port, as well as the provisioning of personnel, fuel (IOTC-2025-CoC22-11_Add4-IOTC Glossary).

#### Fishing set* {#fishingSet}

#### Fishing trip {#fishingTrip}

The period between either (a) a vessel's departure from port after unloading part or all of the catch to transit to a fishing area, or (b) a vessel recommences fishing operations or transits to a fishing area after transshipping part or all of the catch at sea, and the time that the vessel either (c) returns to port to unload part or all of its catch (EM workshop-only WCPFC term).


A defined period during which a vessel engages in fishing activities (EM workshop-workshop standards).

#### Fishing vessel {#fishingVessel}

any vessel of any size used for, equipped for use for, or intended for use for the purposes of fishing or fishing-related activities, including support vessels, fish-processing vessels, vessels engaged in transshipment and carrier vessels equipped for the transportation of fishery products (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Flag state* {#flagState}

The State which has granted to a vessel the right to fly its flag and has issued a registration to that effect (IOTC-2025-CoC22-11_Add4-IOTC Glossary).


State under whose laws a vessel is registered and whose flag it is entitled to fly (IOTC science glossary).

#### Float line {#floatLine}

A rope or line fitted with floats that supports and maintains the position of a fishing gear at the surface or in the water column (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Fork length (FL) {#forkLength}

In a fish with a forked tail, the distance from the mouth tip to the tail fork (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).


Length of a fish measured as the distance between the tip of the snout and the point of the fork or 'V' of the
tail. Commonly used to record the length of commercial fish because it is little affected by damage to the tail fin (c.f. Total
length). Fork length is measured flat, from point to point, not by stretching a tape along the body surface, which would result in a
longer measurement for full-bodied fish like tuna. See also Lower-jaw fork length (IOTC science glossary).

#### Free school {#freeSchool}

A fish school not associated with any anchored or drifting floating object. Synonym to free-swimming school or unassociated school (IOTC glossary).

### G {#G}

#### Galley {#galley}

The kitchen or food preparation area on board a vessel where meals are prepared for the crew and personnel (IMO terminology).

#### Gear {#gear}

The general name for the equipment used for fishing. This might include lines, nets, warps, floats, deck equipment and any other specific fishing items (IOTC glossary).

#### Geolocation device {#geolocationDevice}

A device that is used to capture information on vessel position that can also be used to determine vessel speed and heading (EM workshop-WCPFC term).

#### Ghost fishing gear {#ghostFishingghostGear}

Abandoned fishing gear = fishing gear over which that operator/owner has control and that could be retrieved by owner/operator (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Ghost fishing* {#ghostFishing}

The accidental capture of aquatic organisms by fishing gear (usually gill nets, or traps, pots) (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).


The capture of fish in gear that has been lost, usually nets or traps (IOTC science glossary).

#### Gillnet* {#gillnet}

A net, which is hung vertically in the water so that fish attempting to pass through become caught by the gill covers, entangled or enmeshed in the netting. According to their design, ballasting and buoyancy, these nets may be used to fish on the surface (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).


Type of passive fishing gear consisting of panels of net held vertically in the water column, either in contact with the
seabed or suspended from the sea surface, such that fish attempting to swim through the net are entangled. The mesh size of the
net determines the size range of fish caught, as smaller fish can swim through the meshes and larger fish are not enmeshed. See
also Driftnet (IOTC science glossary).

#### Global maritime distress and safety system (GMDSS) {#globalMaritimeglobalDistressglobalAndglobalSafetyglobalSystem}

An internationally agreed system using satellite and terrestrial communication technologies to ensure that distress alerts, maritime safety information, and emergency communications can be transmitted and received by vessels (IMO terminology).

#### Global navigation satellite system (GNSS) {#globalNavigationglobalSatelliteglobalSystem}

A satellite-based positioning system that provides users with geographic position, navigation, and timing information using signals transmitted from satellites (IMO terminology).

#### Global positioning system (GPS) {#globalPositioningglobalSystem}

a satellite based navigational system allowing the determination of any point on the earth's surface with a high degree of accuracy given a suitable GPS receiver (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Global positioning system plotter {#globalPositioningglobalSystemglobalPlotter}

A navigation device that combines GPS position data with electronic charts to display a vessel's location, track, and planned routes (IMO terminology).

#### Greenwich mean time (GMT) {#greenwichMeangreenwichTime}

The mean solar time at the Greenwich meridian (0� longitude), historically used as the reference time standard for navigation and timekeeping.GMT was formerly used as the international civil time standard, now superseded in that function by Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), defined by a whole number of hours (UTC?12 to UTC+14) (Adapted from IMO terminology).

#### Gross tonnage {#grossTonnage}

A dimensionless measure of the overall internal volume of a vessel, calculated according to the vessel's total enclosed spaces and used to indicate its size (IMO terminology).

### H {#H}

#### Handline* {#handline}

Fishing method in which a line with a hook, usually baited, is lowered into the water from a drifting, anchored or moving fishing vessel or from a jetty (IOTC glossary).


Hand-held lines of various types used to catch fish (IOTC science glossary).

#### Harpoon {#harpoon}

Fishing gear consisting of a pointed dart or iron attached to the end of a line several hundred feet in length (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Hatch {#hatch}

An opening in a ship's deck or structure, fitted with a cover or door, providing access to spaces below or allowing the movement of cargo, equipment, or personnel (IMO terminology).

#### Hatch cover {#hatchCover}

A removable or hinged structure fitted over a hatch opening to close and protect the space below, maintaining the required strength and watertight or weathertight integrity of the deck (IMO terminology).

#### Hauling station {#haulingStation}

The designated area on a fishing vessel where fishing gear is retrieved and brought aboard during hauling operations (Based on FAO terminology).

#### High Frequency Radio (HF radio) {#highFrequencyhighRadio}

A radio communication system that uses high-frequency electromagnetic waves (3-30 MHz) to provide long-range voice and data communication, including maritime safety and operational communications (IMO terminology).

#### High seas* {#highSeas}

All parts of the sea that are not included in the exclusive economic zone, in the territorial sea or in the internal waters of a State (IOTC glossary (UNCLOS)).


that area of the oceans which is not subject to the jurisdiction of any one state.That area of the oceans which is not subject to the jurisdiction of any one state,High seas (FAO terminology portal).

#### Hold {#hold}

A compartment within a vessel used for the storage or carriage of cargo, equipment, or other materials (IMO terminology).

#### Hook pods* {#hookPods}

#### Hull {#hull}

The main body or shell of a vessel that provides its structure, buoyancy, and watertight enclosure (IMO terminology).

### I {#I}

#### Incidentally affected species* {#incidentallyAffectedincidentallySpecies}

Bycatch species that accidentally interact with fishing equipment in the fishery, that are not taken but released to the sea (cetaceans, seals, turtles, birds, etc.). Some of these species may be considered protected, endangered, or threatened (ROS observer manual 2019).

#### Incidentally taken species* {#incidentallyTakenincidentallySpecies}

Bycatch species of no commercial value such as fish species, crustaceans or other non-target organisms without commercial interest, not marketable for reasons of size (immature, juvenile), prohibited from fishing, or from being hauled on-board (ROS observer manual).

#### Industrial fishery {#industrialFishery}

fishery that (i) catches fish from large and medium-sized vessels fitted out with mechanised methods of operating the fishing gear and installations for preservation of fish on board, (ii) process the catch either in land base or on board, in which cases the vessels are provided with appropriate processing installations, and (iii) distribute the fish products around the country and abroad using mechanised means of transportation adapted for fish and fish products. All these activities are generally organised for the financial benefit of the companies or organisations operating the fishing vessels, processing plants (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Industrial fishing vessel* {#industrialFishingindustrialVessel}

Large vessel, typically of 24 m in length and over, engaged in catching operations (IOTC glossary).

#### Industrial fishing* {#industrialFishing}

Using large vessels, generally greater than 15 m in length (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Inmarsat {#inmarsat}

A satellite communication system providing maritime communication services, including voice, data, and safety communications for vessels operating beyond the range of terrestrial communication networks (IMO terminology).

#### Installation coverage {#installationCoverage}

The percentage of vessels equipped with electronic monitoring systems (EM workshop-workshop standards).

#### Instrumented buoy {#instrumentedBuoy}

A buoy with a clearly marked with a unique reference number allowing identification of its owner and equipped with a satellite tracking system to monitor its position (Res. [19/02](https://iotc.org/cmm/resolution-1902-procedures-fish-aggregating-devices-fads-management-plan)) (IOTC resolution 19/02).

#### International maritime organization number (IMO) {#internationalMaritimeinternationalOrganizationinternationalNumber}

A unique seven-digit identification number assigned permanently to a vessel for identification purposes throughout its operational life, regardless of changes in ownership, flag, or name (IMO terminology).

#### International Radio Call Sign (IRCS) {#internationalRadiointernationalCallinternationalSign}

A unique identification signal assigned to a vessel by its flag State administration for use in radio communications (IMO terminology).

#### IOTC active vessel list (AVL) {#iotcActiveiotcVesseliotcList}

The list of vessels having operated in the IOTC area of competence in a given year, including fishing and non-fishing vessels of 24 m length overall and over (IOTC resolution 10/08).

#### IOTC Agreement {#iotcAgreement}

The 1993 Agreement for the establishment of the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission (IOTC data reporting guidelines).

#### IOTC Area of Competence {#iotcAreaiotcOfiotcCompetence}

The Indian Ocean (defined for the purpose of the IOTC Agreement as being FAO Statistical Areas 51 and 57), and adjacent seas, north of the Antarctic Convergence, insofar as it is necessary to cover such seas for the purpose of conserving and managing stocks that migrate into or out of the Indian Ocean. In 1999, the Commission extended the western boundary of the IOTC statistical area from 30ºE to 20ºE (IOTC data reporting guidelines).

#### IOTC Conservation and Management Measures (CMM) {#iotcConservationiotcAndiotcManagementiotcMeasures}

consist of Resolutions, which are binding on Members, subject to Article IX para 5 of the IOTC Agreement, and Recommendations, which are non-binding, as specified in Article IX of the Agreement (IOTC-2025-CoC22-11_Add4-IOTC Glossary).

#### IOTC observer {#iotcObserver}

An observer appointed pursuant to the IOTC Regional Observer Scheme under Resolution 11/04 and Resolution 19/06 and any superseding Resolution (IOTC-2025-CoC22-11_Add4-IOTC Glossary).

#### IOTC Record of Authorized vessels (RAV) {#iotcRecordiotcOfiotcAuthorizediotcVessels}

the list of vessels authorised to operate in the IOTC Area of Competence in a given time period, including fishing and non-fishing vessels of 24 m length overall and over (IOTC data reporting guidelines).

#### IOTC species of special interest {#iotcSpeciesiotcOfiotcSpecialiotcInterest}

Species of Special Interest include all marine turtles, all marine mammals, all seabirds, shark species with a retention ban: whale sharks (Res 13/05), oceanic white tip sharks (Res 13/06) and thresher sharks (Res 12/09.); and billfish species included in Res 18/05: striped, black and blue marlin and Indo-Pacific sailfish (IOTC-2018-SC21-R[E]) (Based on IOTC resolutions).

#### IOTC species* {#iotcSpecies}

Any or all of the 16 tuna and tuna-like species listed in Annex B of the IOTC Agreement (IOTC data reporting guidelines).

#### IOTC stocks {#iotcStocks}

The populations of the IOTC species which are located in the IOTC area of competence or migrate into or out of the area IOTC Agreement (Guidelines for the reporting of fishery statistics to the IOTC).

### L {#L}

#### Landing {#landing}

All transfers of any quantity of fish onboard from a vessel to land, other than transshipment, including transfers of fish to a port facility, transfers of fish from one vessel to another through a port facility or other means of transportation, and transfers of fish from a vessel to a container, truck, train, aircraft (IOTC-2025-CoC22-11_Add4-IOTC Glossary).

#### Large-scale driftnets* {#largeScalelargeDriftnets}

Gillnets or other nets or a combination of nets that are more than 2.5 kilometers in length whose purpose is to enmesh, entrap, or entangle fish by drifting on the surface of, or in, the water column (IOTC science glossary).

#### Large-scale fishery {#largeScalelargeFishery}

Fish is caught by vessels with a length overall of 24 m and above, and sold at landing sites, at markets, to processing factories (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Lead line* {#leadLine}

A weighted line or rope attached to the lower edge of a fishing gear to provide sinking force and maintain the gear's position in the water (Revised from Manual**).

#### Leader {#leader}

The line for attaching hook to the mainline in longlines. The term is often used in drift longlines for pelagic species such as tunas and swordfish (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Length overall (LOA) {#lengthOverall}

The maximum length of a vessel measured in a straight line from the foremost point of the bow to the aftermost point of the stern (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Lift nets {#liftNets}

A lift net is a horizontal netting panel or bag shaped like a parallelepiped, pyramid or cone with the opening facing upwards which are submerged at a certain depth, left for a while, the time necessary for light or bait to attract fish over the opening (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Line fishing {#lineFishing}

A general term used for a range of fishing methods that employ fishing lines in one form or another (as opposed to nets and traps). It includes handlines, hand reels, powered reels, pole-and-line, droplines, longlines, trotlines and troll lines (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Line hauler (branchline) {#lineHaulerlineBranchline}

A branch line hauler/coiler winds branch lines into tight, uniform coils and assists in quickly recovering and packing branch lines for the next set (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Line setter* {#lineSetter}

#### Live weight equivalent {#liveWeightliveEquivalent}

Weight derived from the landed or product weight by the application of certain factors and designed to represent the actual weight of the fishery product as it was taken from the water and before being subjected to any processing or other operations (Eurostat).

#### Longline {#longline}

A fishing gear in which short lines carrying hooks are attached to a longer main line at regular intervals. Longlines are laid on the bottom or suspended horizontally at a predetermined depth with the help of surface floats. The main lines can be as long as 150 km and have several thousand hooks (e.g. in tuna fisheries) (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Longline fisheries {#longlineFisheries}

A fishery undertaken by vessels recorded in the IOTC Record of Authorised Vessels that use a longline gear (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Longline section* {#longlineSection}

#### Lower-jaw fork length {#lowerJawlowerForklowerLength}

Length of a fish measured as the distance between the tip of the lower jaw and the point of the fork or "V" of the tail. Commonly used to record the length of commercial fish with bills (e.g. swordfish) because it is little affected by damage to the tail fin (c.f. Total length) and bill. Fork length is measured flat, from point to point, not by stretching a tape along the body surface (IOTC glossary).


Length of a fish measured as the distance between the tip of the lower jaw and the point of the fork or
'V' of the tail. Commonly used to record the length of commercial fish with bills (e.g. swordfish) because it is little affected by
damage to the tail fin (c.f. Total length) and bill. Fork length is measured flat, from point to point, not by stretching a tape along
the body surface, which would result in a longer measurement for full-bodied fish like tuna (IOTC science glossary).

### M {#M}

#### Magnetic compass {#magneticCompass}

A navigational instrument that indicates a vessel's heading by aligning a magnetized needle or compass card with the Earth's magnetic field (IMO terminology).

#### Mainline {#mainline}

longline fishing gear consists of a mainline kept near the surface or at a particular depth by means of regularly spaced floats or weights. Branchlines with baited hooks are attached to the mainline at regular intervals (IOTC glossary).

#### Medium Frequency Radio (MF radio) {#mediumFrequencymediumRadio}

A radio communication system operating in the medium-frequency band (300 kHz-3 MHz) that provides medium-range voice and digital communications for maritime safety and operational purposes (IMO terminology).

#### Medium-scale fisheries* {#mediumScalemediumFisheries}

Fish is caught in areas beyond national jurisdiction (ABNJ) of the flag state, by vessels with a length overall less than 24 m, and sold at landing sites, at markets, to processing factories (fishery types code list).


the medium scale fishery is generally understood to be a fishery undertaken by powered boats and with small or medium size capital (FAO terminology portal).

#### Meridians {#meridians}

Imaginary lines that run from the North Pole to the South Pole, connecting points of equal longitude and used to measure longitude east or west of the Prime Meridian (IHO terminology).

#### Multiple random sampling* {#multipleRandommultipleSampling}

### N {#N}

#### National jurisdiction areas {#nationalJurisdictionnationalAreas}

Maritime areas over which a coastal State exercises sovereignty or sovereign rights and jurisdiction in accordance with international law (UN definition (UNCLOS)).

#### National jurisdiction areas and beyond {#nationalJurisdictionnationalAreasnationalAndnationalBeyond}

Maritime areas that are either under the sovereignty or jurisdiction of a coastal State, or outside the jurisdiction of any State, as defined under international law (UN definition (UNCLOS)).

#### Nautical twilight {#nauticalTwilight}

The period when the centre of the Sun is between 6� and 12� below the horizon, during which the horizon is still visible at sea and stars suitable for celestial navigation become visible (NOAA).

#### NAVTEX {#navtex}

An automated maritime information service that broadcasts navigational and meteorological warnings, forecasts, and urgent safety information to ships using narrow-band direct-printing radio communication (IMO terminology).

#### Net drum hauler* {#netDrumnetHauler}

#### Net tonnage {#netTonnage}

Dimensionless measure of the useful capacity of a ship (Thermes et al. 2023 (https://www.fao.org/fishery/en/publications/278529)).

#### Nominal catches {#nominalCatches}

officially declared aquatic organisms captured during fisheries and expressed as live weight equivalent. Nominal catches do not include unreported catches, such as unreported discards (Eurostat (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Glossary:Nominal_catch)).

#### Non-target species* {#nonTargetnonSpecies}

species for which the fishing gear is not specifically deployed or set (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).


Species that are unintentionally taken by a fishery or not routinely assessed for fisheries management. See
also Bycatch, Byproduct (IOTC science glossary).

### O {#O}

#### Observer {#observer}

means a person who collects information on board fishing vessels, in the framework of observer programs, and can be used inter alia for monitoring fishing activities, quantifying species composition of target species and bycatch (Resolution 25/06).

#### Offal {#offal}

the viscera and trimmings of a butchered animal removed in preparing it for market or for consumption (Webster dictionary definition).

#### Onboard interface {#onboardInterface}

An on-board screen, or equivalent interface, to allow verification by the master/crew of the correct functioning of the system is required (EM workshop standards).

#### Operational buoy {#operationalBuoy}

any instrumented buoy, previously activated, switched on and deployed at sea on a drifting FAD or log (Resolution 19/02 (https://iotc.org/cmm/resolution-1902-procedures-fish-aggregating-devices-fads-management-plan)).

### P {#P}

#### Pelagic {#pelagic}

Inhabiting surface waters rather than the sea floor. Usually applied to free-swimming species such as tunas and sharks (c.f. Demersal) (IOTC science glossary).


Relating to, living or occurring in the open sea (FAO terminology portal).

#### Pole-and-line fishing (poling) {#poleAndpoleLinepoleFishingpolePoling}

a fishing technique in which surface schooling fish are attracted to the vessel and driven into very active feeding behaviour by throwing live or dead bait into the water and spraying water onto the sea surface to simulate the escape behaviour of small preys. The fish lured with a line and a hook attached to a pole and pulled off the water by manual or powered devices,Pole-and-line fishing (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).


Fishing method in which fishers attract schools of fish to the vessel with live or dead bait, get
them into a feeding frenzy with more bait and water sprayed onto the sea surface to simulate the behaviour of small baitfish, and
then use poles with short, fixed lines and lures to 'pole' the fish aboard (IOTC science glossary).

#### Pole-and-lines {#poleAndpoleLines}

consists of a hooked line attached to a pole. This method is common to sport fisheries (angling) but it is also used in commercial fisheries. Fishing rods/poles are made of wood (including bamboo, also constructed of split cane) and increasingly of fiberglass (IOTC data catalogue fishery categories).

#### Pool of observers {#poolOfpoolObservers}

means a list of IOTC recognised observers that have been allocated an IOTC registration number and trained according to IOTC standards who may be called upon by other flag States (IOTC Resolution 25/06).

#### Port {#port}

A place on the coast or shore where vessels can enter, anchor, load, unload cargo or catch, receive services, and carry out other maritime activities (IMO term).

#### Port of registration {#portOfportRegistration}

The port recorded in a vessel's registration documents as the official port associated with the vessel's registration under its flag State (IMO term).

#### Power block {#powerBlock}

A mechanized pulley used to haul in nets, purse seine, etc (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Purse line* {#purseLine}

#### Purse seine {#purseSeine}

nets characterized by the use of a purse line at the bottom of the net. The purse line enables the net to be closed like a purse and thus retain all the fish caught. The purse seines, which may be very large, are operated by one or two boats. The most usual case is a purse seine operated by a single boat (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Purse seine bunt* {#purseSeinepurseBunt}

#### Purse seine tackle* {#purseSeinepurseTackle}

#### Purse seining {#purseSeining}

harvesting of surface-schooling pelagic fish by surrounding the school with a net. A line that passes through rings on the bottom of the net can be tightened to close the net so that the fish cannot escape,Purse seining (IOTC glossary).

### R {#R}

#### Radar {#radar}

short for radio detection and ranging. A system of detecting and locating targets which are capable of reflecting high frequency radio waves (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Retained catches {#retainedCatches}

estimated component of the catch which is retained on board during a fishing trip (CWP (https://www.fao.org/cwp-on-fishery-statistics/handbook/capture-fisheries-statistics/catch-and-landings/en/)).

#### Review for data quality {#reviewForreviewDatareviewQuality}

The verification process of re-analysing/interpreting a portion of previously analysed electronic monitoring (EM) records to determine completeness, adherence to protocols (EM workshop-WCPFC term).

#### Ring nets {#ringNets}

A ring net is a net the form of which is intermediate hybrid between a purse seine and a lamapara net: like on a purse seine, rings at the lower edge of the net, allow using a purse line to close it under the fish (pursing) and like on a lampara net (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Round weight {#roundWeight}

weight of the whole fish before processing or removal of any part (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

### S {#S}

#### Search and rescue transponder (SART) {#searchAndsearchRescuesearchTransponder}

A radar transponder carried by survival craft or vessels that responds to search radar signals by transmitting a series of pulses, allowing rescuers to locate survivors during search and rescue operations (IMO terminology).


These devices may be either a radar-SART (Search and Rescue Transponder), or an AIS-SART (AIS Search and Rescue Transmitter) are used to locate survival craft or distressed vessels by creating a series of dots on a rescuing ship's 3 cm radar display (observer manual 2019).

#### Semi-industrial fishery {#semiIndustrialsemiFishery}

Fishery that (i) catches fish from medium- (and/or small-) sized vessels fitted out with mechanised methods of operating the fishing gear, (ii) process the catch in land bases, and (iii) distributed the fish and fish products around a limited area, and in exceptional cases only for export. These activities are aimed at the financial benefit of the companies or organisations operating the fishing vessels, processing plants (Thermes et al. 2023 (https://www.fao.org/fishery/en/publications/278529)).

#### Semi-industrial fishing vessel {#semiIndustrialsemiFishingsemiVessel}

medium-sized vessel, typically of 12 m in length but less than 24 m in length, engaged in catching operations (Thermes et al. 2023 (https://www.fao.org/fishery/en/publications/278529)).


commercial fishing vessel of length overall comprised between 15 and 24 m and exclusively operating in the exclusive economic zone of the flag state (([IOTC-2023-WPDCS19-07_Rev1](https://iotc.org/documents/WPDCS/19/07))).

#### Sensors {#sensors}

#### Set gillnets {#setGillnets}

a set gillnet is a long rectangular netting anchored or otherwise fixed to the seabed to catch fish when they come in contact with it. The set gillnet is held open vertically in the water by a headrope usually with floats, and by a footrope weighted with sinkers. Floatation and weight may be built into ropes, which are usually called floatrope and leadrope respectively. The net is kept in position by anchors or other weights, usually at both ends (IOTC reference fish categories).

#### Set longline {#setLongline}

A longline gear that is anchored or otherwise fixed to the seabed at either end of the mainline (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Shallow setting* {#shallowSetting}

the gear is deployed at a shallow depth (gear configuration code lists).

#### Shark line {#sharkLine}

Branch lines running directly off the longline floats or drop lines made from material resistant to shark bites, such as wire or other strong materials, used to reduce the likelihood of sharks biting through the line (IOTC) (IOTC).

#### Sinker {#sinker}

a weight used to sink a fishing line or net (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Size frequency {#sizeFrequency}

the number of individuals in a catch or catch sample in each group of sizes (size intervals) (IOTC data reporting guidelines).


See Length-frequency distribution (IOTC science glossary).

#### Small-scale fishery* {#smallScalesmallFishery}

Fishery characterised in most cases by fishing vessels with non-mechanized propulsion systems (sails and oars) or low-horsepower outboard or inboard engines, use of passive fishing methods, manual operation of fishing gear (setting, shooting and hauling) and the absence of electronic fish-finding and navigational devices ([Tietze et al. 2000](https://www.fao.org/3/x8294e/X8294E00.htm)). From a socio-economic perspective, small-scale fisheries can be broadly categorised as a dynamic and evolving sector employing labour intensive harvesting, processing and distribution technologies to exploit marine and inland water fishery resources. The activities of this sub-sector, conducted full-time or part-time, or just seasonally, are often targeted on supplying fish and fishery products to local and domestic markets (IOTC data reporting guidelines).

#### Sonar {#sonar}

an apparatus that uses sound waves to detect objects underwater by measuring or classifying the echoes received from them. An echo sounder is a sonar that transmits vertically. In practice, a sonar is an apparatus other than an echo sounder, i.e (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Species of special interest {#speciesOfspeciesSpecialspeciesInterest}

Species of Special Interest include all marine turtles, all marine mammals, all seabirds, shark species with a retention ban: whale sharks (Res 13/05), oceanic white tip sharks (Res 13/06) and thresher sharks (Res 12/09.); and billfish species included in Res 18/05: striped (Adapted from IOTC resolutions).

#### Standard length {#standardLength}

The length of fish measured in a straight line from the tip of the snout to the end of the caudal skeleton (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Stow nets {#stowNets}

A stow net is a stationary gear made from netting, usually in the form of a cone or pyramid. Stow nets can be fixed for a long time at the same place in rows. These nets are fixed by means of anchors or stakes, placed according to the direction and strength of the current. The mouths are sometimes held open by a frame (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Stratified sampling {#stratifiedSampling}

A sampling method in which the population or catch is divided into predefined, mutually exclusive strata, from each of which samples are selected separately.

#### Streamer lines {#streamerLines}

Lines fitted with streamers that are towed from a fishing vessel to deter seabirds from approaching baited hooks or fishing gear and reduce seabird interactions. Synonym to "Tori lines" (IOTC).

#### Sub-surface setting {#subSurfacesubSetting}

The gear is deployed beyond the surface of the water (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Subsistence fishery {#subsistenceFishery}

Fish is caught in national jurisdiction areas (NJA) of the flag state, by vessels with a length overall of less than 15 m (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Supply vessel {#supplyVessel}

Any vessel used, equipped to be used or intended to be used for purse seine fishing related activities, including any vessel, other than a craft, carried on board a fishing vessel that is not equipped with operational fishing gear and that facilitates. Synonym to "Support vessel" (IOTC-2025-CoC22-11_Add4-IOTC Glossary).


Non-fishing vessel supporting fishing operations and in particular assisting purse seine fishing vessels in the location of tuna schools and in the the deployment, monitoring and retrieving of buoys and drifting fish aggregating devices. Synonym to supply vessel (IOTC data reporting guidelines).

#### Support vessel {#supportVessel}

Any vessel used, equipped to be used or intended to be used for purse seine fishing related activities, including any vessel, other than a craft, carried on board a fishing vessel that is not equipped with operational fishing gear and that facilitates. Synonym to "Supply vessel" (IOTC-2025-CoC22-11_Add4-IOTC Glossary).


Fishing support vessels receive the catch of fishing vessels and supply vessels that bring fuel and provisions to fishing vessels (FAO terminology portal).

#### Surface fishery {#surfaceFishery}

All fisheries operated by vessels in the IOTC Record of Authorized Vessels other than longline fisheries; in particular purse seine, pole-and-line, gillnet fisheries (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).


0 ((Res. [15/02](https://www.iotc.org/cmm/resolution-1502-mandatory-statistical-reporting-requirements-iotc-contracting-parties-and))).

#### Systematic proportional sampling {#systematicProportionalsystematicSampling}

Individuals are selected systematically, with sample sizes proportional to the abundance of species or catch components in the catch (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

### T {#T}

#### Target species {#targetSpecies}

Species that are primarily sought in a particular fishery and are the subject of directed fishing effort. There may be primary and secondary target species (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Tonnage {#tonnage}

A measure of the size or capacity of a ship (Thermes et al. 2023 (https://www.fao.org/fishery/en/publications/278529)).

#### Tori lines {#toriLines}

Lines fitted with streamers that are towed from a fishing vessel to deter seabirds from approaching baited hooks or fishing gear and reduce seabird interactions. Synonym to "Streamer lines" (IOTC).

#### Track plotter {#trackPlotter}

A device or software tool used to display, record, or plot the movement of a vessel over time, based on its geographical positions (IOTC).

#### Trawl {#trawl}

A trawl is a cone-shaped net (made from two, four or more panels) which is towed, by one or two boats, on the bottom or in midwater (pelagic). The cone-shaped body ends in a bag or coded. The horizontal opening of the gear while it is towed is maintained by beams, otter boards or by the distance between the two towing vessels (pair trawling). Floats and weights and/or hydrodynamic devices provide for the vertical opening. Two parallel trawls might be rigged between two otter boards (twin trawls). The mesh size in the codend or special designed devices is used to regulate the size and species to be captured (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Trolling line {#trollingLine}

A trolling line consists of a line with natural or artificial baited hooks and is trailed by a vessel near the surface or at a certain depth. Several lines are often towed at the same time, by using outriggers to keep the lines away from the wake of the vessel. The line are hauled by hand or with small winches. A piece of rubber is often included in each line as a shock absorber (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).


A line with one or more baited hooks (or lures) towed behind a boat (FAO terminology portal).

### U {#U}

#### Unfit for human consumption {#unfitForunfitHumanunfitConsumption}

Fish that are not suitable for human consumption because they have been meshed or crushed in the purse seine, damaged due to depredation, or have died and spoiled in the net following a gear failure that prevents normal retrieval of the net and catch and efforts to release the fish alive. This does not include fish considered undesirable in terms of size, marketability, or species composition, or fish spoiled or contaminated as a result of an act or omission of the fishing vessel crew (IOTC).

#### Uninterruptable power supply (UPS) {#uninterruptablePoweruninterruptableSupply}

Provides power to the system and enables controlled shutdown in the event of a power loss so as to preserve the security and integrity of data (EM workshop-WCPFC term only).

#### Upper-jaw fork length (FL) {#upperJawupperForkupperLength}

Straight distance between the tip of the upper jaw and the fork of the tail (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

### V {#V}

#### Vertical lines {#verticalLines}

A vertical line consists of a line to which is attached sinker and one or several hooks. In commercial fisheries the lines have usually several hooks. The additional hooks can be fixed on the mainline at short intervals with branch lines of a certain length. The line weighed down by sinkers can be set up to 200 m depth and is hauled with jerky movements (IOTC Reference Data Catalogue).

#### Very high frequency radios (VHF) {#veryHighveryFrequencyveryRadios}

A marine radio communication system that operates in the very high frequency band (30-300 MHz), commonly used for short-range voice communication between vessels, shore stations, and maritime safety services (IMO terminology).

#### Vessel monitoring plan {#vesselMonitoringvesselPlan}

The vessel's Electronic Monitoring (EM) equipment characteristics and how the vessel's EM equipment is installed and configured to monitor fishing activities and meet the EM Programme and EM Data Standards as required by the IOTC Regional Electronic Monitoring (EM workshop).

#### Vessel monitoring system {#vesselMonitoringvesselSystem}

A secure satellite-based monitoring system capable of transmitting the position and identity of vessels to the competent authorities (IOTC-2025-CoC22-11_Add4-IOTC Glossary).

#### Vessel Monitoring System (VMS) {#vesselMonitoringvesselSystem}

A satellite-based monitoring system which at regular intervals provides data to fisheries authorities on the location (FAO terminology (https://www.fao.org/faoterm/en/)).

#### Vessel name {#vesselName}

The name by which a vessel is officially registered or identified by the relevant authority (Adapted from FAO, Manual on sample-based data collection for fisheries assessment).

#### Vessel operator {#vesselOperator}

Any person who is in charge of, directs or controls a vessel (EM workshop-WCFPC term only).

### W {#W}

#### Winch (and seine arrow)* {#winchAndwinchSeinewinchArrow}

A powerful machine with one or more drums on which to coil a rope, cable, or chain for hauling or hoisting (Webster dictionary definition).
